report.summary: Section 8 defines a loop but omits definitions for ExperimentSpec, Forest, Context Capsule, evaluation cascade, receipt, sealed path, and interaction experiment, forcing implementers to guess their semantics.
risks: 8.1 | high | 'ExperimentSpec' is undefined; an implementer cannot know what fields or constraints it carries. | Check whether any part of the document defines ExperimentSpec. If not, the claim is unenforceable.
8.2 | high | 'Forest' is undefined; its structure, construction rules, and validity criteria are absent. | Check whether Forest is defined elsewhere; if not, implementers must guess.

8.3 | high | 'formulation', 'parent', 'operator axis', 'model', 'evaluation fidelity' are undefined. The selection step cannot be implemented without knowing permissible values. | Search for definitions of these terms; absence forces arbitrary interpretation.
8.4 | high | 'Context Capsule' is undefined; its composition and verification rules are missing. | Check document for Context Capsule definition; if absent, step 4 is ambiguous.
8.5 | medium | 'isolated, capability-bounded trial' lacks definition of isolation and capability bounds. | Determine what constitutes isolation and bounds; without it, reproducibility is compromised.

8.6 | low | 'content-addressed storage' is a known concept but the document doesn't specify the addressing scheme or storage backend. | Implementer must choose a scheme; risk of incompatibility if multiple implementations differ.
8.7 | medium | 'revision-aware delta' is undefined; its format and computation method are not described. | Check for delta definition; without it, step 7 is ambiguous.

8.8 | high | 'evaluation cascade' is undefined; the ordering and conditions for 'cheap validity checks to held-out tests' are unspecified. | Document must define the cascade stages and pass/fail criteria; absence forces guesswork.

8.9 | medium | 'signed/traceable receipt' requires a signing mechanism and traceability scheme not defined. | Identify what constitutes a receipt and how it is signed; missing details undermine auditability.

8.10 | medium | 'never auto-promote them' is clear but the mechanism that prevents auto-promotion is not defined; relies on undefined 'sealed owner-controlled path'. | Show that the system enforces no auto-promotion; without defined path, rule is unenforceable.

8.11 | high | 'sealed owner-controlled path' is undefined; no authentication, authorization, or sealing mechanism is described. | Attempt to promote via any path; if no sealed path exists, promotion is undefined.

8.12 | medium | 'pre-registered interaction experiment' is undefined; its registration process and justification criteria are missing. | Check for definition of interaction experiment; without it, the exception is unenforceable.

8.13 | medium | 'do not silently co-evolve' is a rule but no mechanism to detect or prevent silent co-evolution is specified. | Show a campaign where two axes change without registration; without detection, rule is aspirational.
todos: Define ExperimentSpec, Forest, Context Capsule, evaluation cascade, receipt format, sealed path, and interaction experiment.
Specify the fields and constraints of ExperimentSpec.
Define Forest structure and construction rules.
Define formulation, parent, operator axis, model, and evaluation fidelity with permissible values.
Define Context Capsule composition and verification.
Define isolation and capability bounds for trials.
Define evaluation cascade stages and pass/fail criteria.
Define receipt signing and traceability mechanism.
Define sealed owner-controlled promotion path with authentication and authorization.
Define interaction experiment registration and justification process.
Specify mechanism to detect or prevent silent co-evolution.

claims.claim: Freeze an ExperimentSpec, budget, tasks, metrics, baselines, and seed policy.
claims.why: ExperimentSpec is not defined; an implementer cannot know its structure or what freezing entails. The document omits the definition of a central concept.

claims.claim: Build the base Forest for an exact source revision.
claims.why: Forest is not defined; its structure, construction rules, and validity criteria are absent. The claim assumes a known entity that is not specified.

claims.claim: Select formulation, parent, one operator axis, model, and evaluation fidelity.
claims.why: None of these terms (formulation, parent, operator axis, model, evaluation fidelity) are defined. The selection step cannot be implemented without knowing permissible values or semantics.

claims.claim: Compile a minimal Context Capsule from verified project evidence.
claims.why: Context Capsule is not defined; its composition, minimality criteria, and verification rules are missing. The claim requires a concept that has no specification.
Isolation and capability bounds are not defined. An implementer must guess what constitutes isolation and how capabilities are bounded, leading to inconsistent interpretations.

claims.claim: Store the candidate source tree in content-addressed storage.
claims.why: Content-addressed storage is a well-known concept. While the specific scheme is not detailed, the claim is operational and implementable with standard choices.

claims.claim: Build a candidate Forest and revision-aware delta.
claims.why: Forest is undefined (see 8.2), and 'revision-aware delta' is not defined. The format and computation of the delta are unspecified, forcing implementers to invent a representation.

claims.claim: Run the evaluation cascade from cheap validity checks to held-out tests.
claims.why: 'Evaluation cascade' is not defined; the ordering, stages, and pass/fail criteria are absent. An implementer cannot know what constitutes the cascade or how to progress through it.

claims.claim: Emit a signed/traceable receipt and archive all outcomes.
claims.why: The receipt format, signing mechanism, and traceability scheme are not defined. Without these, the claim is aspirational; implementers must guess how to sign and trace.

claims.claim: Nominate successful candidates; never auto-promote them.
claims.why: The prohibition is clear, but the mechanism that prevents auto-promotion is not defined. The claim relies on an undefined 'sealed owner-controlled path' (see 8.11) to enforce it.

claims.claim: Promote only through the sealed owner-controlled path.
claims.why: 'Sealed owner-controlled path' is not defined. No authentication, authorization, or sealing mechanism is described. An implementer cannot build or identify this path.

claims.claim: Campaigns factorize evolution: change one major axis at a time unless a pre-registered interaction experiment justifies more.
claims.why: 'Pre-registered interaction experiment' is not defined; its registration process, justification criteria, and how it overrides the factorization rule are absent.

claims.claim: Code, prompts, operators, evaluators, and orchestration do not silently co-evolve in one campaign.
claims.why: The rule prohibits silent co-evolution but provides no mechanism to detect or prevent it. Without monitoring or enforcement, the claim is unenforceable.
